title: Variational Quantum Transformer Architecture for Synthetic Language Generation
authors: Julian Hager, Michael Kölle, Gerhard Stenzel, Tobias Rohe, Jonas Stein, Claudia Linnhoff-Popien
abstract: We propose a compact NISQ-compatible quantum transformer architecture for synthetic QNLP sequence modelling. The model preserves the autoregressive next-token interface of a classical transformer, but replaces attention and feed-forward sublayers with variational quantum encoder blocks, connector circuits, decoder blocks and a direct two-qubit measurement readout. Token contexts are angle-encoded into small quantum registers, processed by parallel variational heads and encoder integration circuits and conditioned through decoder ancillae to produce a distribution over a four-token vocabulary. We evaluate several architecture variants on deterministic and lexicographic grammar-generation tasks against a compact classical transformer baseline. The quantum models are trainable end-to-end and learn nontrivial grammar structure, including perfect deterministic generation in individual runs and high lexicographic validity in the strongest variant. The classical baseline remains more accurate and stable and the quantum models are sensitive to initialization. The contribution is therefore not a claim of quantum advantage, but a concrete architecture and evaluation of transformer-inspired QNLP sequence modelling under near-term quantum constraints.
summary: This paper introduces a variational quantum transformer designed for sequence modeling in QNLP, replacing classical layers with quantum circuits. The authors demonstrate that the architecture can learn complex grammar rules, though performance comparisons show that a classical transformer remains more accurate and stable. The work serves as a proof-of-concept for applying quantum circuits to structured data generation under near-term quantum constraints.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of developing a compact, NISQ-compatible quantum architecture for performing synthetic Quantum Natural Language Processing (QNLP) sequence modeling.
main_result: While the quantum models successfully learn nontrivial grammar regularities, the classical transformer baseline remained more accurate and stable, indicating the current work is a feasibility study rather than a claim of quantum advantage.
method: The authors propose a variational quantum transformer that replaces classical attention/feed-forward layers with variational quantum blocks, trained end-to-end using negative log-likelihood loss.
model_or_system: The system is a hybrid quantum-classical model featuring an autoregressive structure. It uses angle-encoding for tokens and consists of variational quantum encoder, connector, and decoder blocks.
key_observables: Token accuracy and a comprehensive grammar score evaluating structural validity on deterministic and lexicographic grammars.
important_parameters: The architecture depth (E, D, V) and the number of trainable parameters (e.g., 354–364 for quantum vs. 700 for classical).
main_assumptions: The contribution is explicitly framed as an architectural demonstration under NISQ constraints, acknowledging that the classical baseline is superior in performance and stability.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the mean grammar score comparison across various quantum and classical models for both deterministic and lexicographic tasks over multiple seeds.
paper_structure: The paper details the architectural design, including circuit components (encoding, encoder blocks, connector, decoder blocks), presents the experimental evaluation on controlled grammar tasks, and concludes by comparing performance against a classical baseline.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, near-term quantum circuit implementation for a complex machine learning task (NLP), which is highly relevant for researchers exploring quantum machine learning algorithms on current hardware.
